title: Zoning for a glass studio: districts, special use permits, historic district review, zoning permit and certificate of occupancy
question: Where in Staunton can a hot glass studio with retail and classes go, what zoning approvals does it need, and what changes if the building is in a downtown historic district?
office: Community Development Department, Planning & Zoning Division (the Zoning Administrator, who is also the Historic Preservation Coordinator; staff to the Planning Commission, the Historic Preservation Commission and the Board of Zoning Appeals); City Council decides uses permitted on review
summary: Staunton's zoning code (City Code Title 18, on eCode360) has no use called glass studio. A hot shop is manufacturing, a gallery is retail and classes are instruction, so the fit depends on the district. The B-2 general business district permits processing and manufacturing that is not objectionable for smoke, odor, dust or noise only when it is incidental to a retail business on the premises and employs no more than ten people in production, and allows a larger enclosed manufacturing use on review (a special use permit: $250, pre-application meeting, public hearings before the Planning Commission and City Council, about three months). The I-1 light industrial district permits making articles from glass inside an enclosed building but allows retail only when it serves industrial plants. The B-1 local business district lists retail, restaurants, small repair shops and schools but no manufacturing. Five historic districts (Gospel Hill, Beverley, The Wharf, Stuart Addition and Newtown) carry the H-1 overlay: any material exterior change visible from a public street, including signs, vents and stacks, needs a Certificate of Appropriateness, by staff review for signs and mechanical screening (about ten business days) or by the Historic Preservation Commission (fourth Tuesday; agenda deadline the first Tuesday). A zoning permit ($50) and, for a new use in an existing building, a certificate of occupancy from the Building Official complete the zoning side. Apply in the online portal; talk to Planning & Zoning (540.332.3862) first.

For the granting of special exceptions under suitable regulations and safeguards; notwithstanding any other provisions of this article, the governing body of any locality may reserve unto itself the right to issue such special exceptions.

The zoning administrator shall respond within 90 days of a request for a decision or determination on zoning matters within the scope of his authority unless the requester has agreed to a longer period.

For the collection of fees to cover the cost of making inspections, issuing permits, advertising of notices and other expenses incident to the administration of a zoning ordinance or to the filing or processing of any appeal or amendment thereto.

The local planning commission shall not recommend nor the governing body adopt any plan, ordinance or amendment thereof until notice of intention to do so has been published twice in some newspaper published or having general circulation in the locality, with the first notice appearing no more than 28 days before and the second notice appearing no less than five days before the date of the meeting referenced in the notice

The ordinance may include a provision that no building or structure, including signs, shall be erected, reconstructed, altered, or restored within any such district unless approved by the review board or, on appeal, by the governing body of the locality as being architecturally compatible with the historic landmarks, buildings, or structures therein.

steps.step: Find the zoning district and overlays of the building
steps.how: Look the address up on the city's GIS map (the Planning & Zoning page links the City GIS Map and a map that answers whether a property is in a historic district), or ask Planning & Zoning. Staunton has 17 district classifications (City Code § 18.15.010): the ones a studio is likely to meet are B-1 local business, B-2 general business, B-3 and B-4 planned business, B-5 mixed-use business, P-1 professional, I-1 light industrial, I-2 heavy industrial and I-3 planned industrial, plus the H-1 historic preservation overlay and the Entrance Corridor Overlay District on 13 corridors. The Entrance Corridor design guidelines (including sign guidelines) are recommendations adopted by Council, not law, but the overlay chapter (§ 18.83) sets standards for height, signage, landscaping and utility placement.
steps.quote: The Entrance Corridor Overlay District is composed of 13 corridors, with 10 of them leading into historic districts in the City.

steps.step: Match the studio to the district's permitted uses (the Zoning Administrator decides)
steps.who: Studio owner; Zoning Administrator (Planning & Zoning Division)
steps.how: Read the district chapter on eCode360 (links in legal_basis) and take the equipment and use list to the Zoning Administrator. As read on 2026-10-19: B-1 (ch. 18.55) permits retail stores, restaurants and tea rooms, custom trades and repair shops with up to five persons, and schools, but no manufacturing; B-2 (ch. 18.60) permits processing and manufacturing that is not objectionable because of smoke, odor, dust or noise, but only when incidental to a retail business on the premises with no more than ten persons employed in the processing, and permits business and vocational schools that are not industrial in character; I-1 (ch. 18.75) permits, inside a completely enclosed building, making articles from previously prepared materials that include glass, but allows retail or service uses only when they serve industrial plants or their employees. A gallery-first studio with a small hot shop and classes therefore reads most naturally as a B-2 retail use with incidental processing; a production shop with wholesale output reads as I-1, where the public side is the problem. Ask for the determination in writing (Zoning Verification Letter, ten business days, $75) if you need it for a lease or lender; state law gives the Zoning Administrator 90 days to answer a request for a determination.
steps.deadline: Zoning Administrator's determination within 90 days of a written request (Va. Code § 15.2-2286(A)(4)); city estimate ten business days for a Zoning Verification Letter
steps.quote: Once the request has been completed, the applicant will receive the zoning verification by email.

steps.step: If the use is permitted on review, apply for a special use permit
steps.who: Studio owner (or a buyer under contract, with the contract attached); Planning & Zoning; Planning Commission (hearing and recommendation); City Council (decision)
steps.how: A pre-application meeting with Planning staff is required or the application will not be accepted. Then apply in the online portal (or on the paper Application for Special Use Permit) with the $250 fee, a plat or map, a detailed description of the proposed use, floor plans and, if you will change the exterior or build, drawings; the form asks which zoning code section lists the use as permitted on review and whether public utilities are adequate. The ordinance (ch. 18.210, read on eCode360) has the application show the site, intended use and the owners and uses within 200 feet, requires a published 10-day notice of the Planning Commission's public hearing, lets the Commission attach conditions, and sends the use to City Council for approval; state law requires two published notices for the hearings. The city estimates three months and asks applicants to check the meeting dates and submittal deadlines. Once Council approves, the certificate is emailed and the building official issues the building permit subject to the conditions.
steps.deadline: City estimate about three months; the ordinance says uses permitted on review are decided within 45 days of application (ch. 18.210, read)
steps.quote: Required Information: Plat/Map of Property, Plan Submittal (detailed description of request), floor plans, if necessary for special use permits.

steps.step: If the building is in a historic district, get a Certificate of Appropriateness for exterior work and signs
steps.who: Property owner or agent; Planning & Zoning staff (administrative review); Historic Preservation Commission (Commission review)
steps.how: Check the map. In the H-1 overlay (ch. 18.85, read on eCode360) no material change affecting the appearance of a building in a district, including construction, exterior alteration, demolition or relocation, may be made until a Certificate of Appropriateness is approved, and the certificate is required whether or not a building permit is; ordinary maintenance is exempt and the Commission does not review interior work. For a hot shop that means furnace flues, exhaust stacks, rooftop or wall-mounted ventilation and gas equipment visible from the street, new doors or loading openings, storefront changes and signs. The city's application offers two routes: administrative review by staff (about ten business days) for signage, screening of mechanical equipment, removing vinyl or metal siding, half-round gutters and in-kind roof replacement over half a roof element; and Commission review for everything else, on the fourth Tuesday at 5:30 p.m. in Council Chambers, with the applicant present and the complete application and fee in by the first Tuesday (the 2026 schedule lists each month's deadline and meeting). Submit sketches or elevations, a site plan or plat, photographs and a materials list (digital plans to permits@fileshare.ci.staunton.va.us). The ordinance encourages a pre-application conference with staff. Approvals run 12 months (one extension of up to a year on written request) and lapse if work stops for 12 months. The Historic District Design Guidelines apply.
steps.deadline: Complete application and fee by the first Tuesday of the month for that month's Commission meeting; approval expires 12 months after it is granted
steps.fee: Not stated on the fee schedule read; ask Planning & Zoning
steps.quote: There are two application processes for work being completed in a historic district: Administrative and Commission Review.

steps.step: Get the zoning permit for the use and check parking and screening
steps.how: The Planning & Zoning fee schedule (and § 18.220.020) lists a $50 zoning permit fee; zoning permits are applied for in the online portal under Zoning Permits. Minimum off-street parking (ch. 18.125) and landscaping and screening rules apply to the use and any site change; in the I-1 district a building may not be built within 50 feet of a residential district and outdoor storage must be screened. If exterior site work or a new building is involved, a Site Plan for Commercial Development ($200, about 45 days for the first review; the VESMP stormwater plan is submitted with it) goes through the Development Review process, and the Plan Submittal Form asks whether the property is in an Entrance Corridor, Historic Preservation District or the Enterprise Zone.
steps.fee: Zoning permit $50.00; site plan submittal or resubmittal $200.00 if a site plan is required

steps.step: Get a sign permit (or a Certificate of Appropriateness for signage in a historic district)
steps.who: Studio owner or sign contractor; Planning & Zoning Division; Building Services for structural or electrical sign work
steps.how: Outside the historic districts, apply for a sign permit online or on the paper Sign Permit Application with a site sketch showing locations and setbacks for freestanding signs and sign plans with dimensions, placement on the building and a night view for internally lit cabinet signs; the city estimates ten business days and requires a final inspection. Inside a historic district, apply instead for a Certificate of Appropriateness for signage (administrative review). The sign application warns that some signs also need a building permit or an electrical permit; City Code § 15.10.120 (read on eCode360) sets a $95 building permit per sign and $75 for sign electrical work, and § 15.10.100 requires a bond before a sign that needs a building code permit is erected. Entrance corridor sign guidelines apply on the 13 corridors.
steps.fee: Sign building permit $95.00 per sign and sign electrical permit $75.00 where the building code applies (City Code § 15.10.120, read on eCode360); zoning sign permit fee not stated on the schedule read
steps.quote: Please be aware that certain signs may require a separate

steps.step: Get the certificate of occupancy for the new use before opening
steps.who: Studio owner; Building Services Division (the Building Official issues it); Zoning Administrator and Planning & Zoning (use requirements and field inspection)
steps.how: City Code § 18.205.010 (read on eCode360) bars occupying a new building or changing the occupancy of an existing one until the building official issues a certificate of occupancy, and the state building code says the same. Apply in the online portal under Change of Use / Occupancy / Existing Bldg CO with a building plan or floor plan; the city estimates ten business days for residential and fifteen for commercial. The Start a Business page says the Zoning Administrator, the inspections division and Planning will set the requirements for the proposed use and arrange the field inspection. The fee for a certificate of occupancy for an existing building is $95 under § 15.10.120 (read on eCode360). Where the change of use needs construction, the certificate comes after the final inspections (see glass_studio_building_mechanical). Delinquent real estate taxes on the property block any zoning or building approval (§ 18.195.040, read).
steps.deadline: Before the studio is occupied; the building official issues the certificate within five working days after the final inspection is approved
steps.fee: Certificate of occupancy for an existing building $95.00 (City Code § 15.10.120, read on eCode360)
steps.quote: You may be required to have an occupancy permit issued by the Zoning Administrator.

steps.step: If the district does not fit at all: rezoning, zoning text amendment, or a different site
steps.who: Studio owner; Planning & Zoning; Planning Commission; City Council
steps.how: A rezoning ($250) or a zoning text amendment (fee due only once the Planning Commission authorizes the amendment; about four months) both need a pre-application meeting and public hearings before the Planning Commission and City Council. A text amendment that names artisan or craft manufacturing with retail and instruction in the business districts is the long route; a different building in a district that fits is usually the short one. The Department of Economic Development keeps a property search for available sites.
steps.deadline: Rezoning about three months; zoning text amendment about four months (city estimates)
steps.fee: Rezoning $250.00; zoning text amendment per the fee schedule, payable after the Planning Commission authorizes the amendment
steps.quote: A zoning text amendment must receive authorization from Planning Commission before it can be considered. Once Planning Commission approves the authorization, it will be set to have public hearings by Planning Commission and City Council.

caveats: City pages and PDFs are Internet Archive copies (dates in sources); the Historic Preservation Districts page is a 2021 capture. The live pages may have changed.

Local law not quoted. The zoning chapters were read on eCode360 on 2026-10-19 and are paraphrased; eCode360's terms forbid reproducing its text for public purposes. Confirm the wording on eCode360 (links in legal_basis) or with Planning & Zoning.

No district lists a glass studio, artisan manufacturing, a craft school or a makerspace. The readings above are lexflow's; the Zoning Administrator's determination governs. The B-2 'incidental to a retail business' and 'not more than 10 persons' limits, and the I-1 limit on retail, are the two tests most likely to decide the question.
The B-3, B-5 and I-3 planned districts and the P-1 and TND districts were not read; their chapters are linked from the Title 18 contents (https://ecode360.com/49104063).
The Certificate of Appropriateness fee is not on the Planning & Zoning fee schedule read, and the zoning fee for a sign permit is not listed; ask the office.

Chapter 18.210 (read) says uses permitted on review are decided within 45 days of application, while the city's page estimates three months for the hearings; treat the 45 days as the ordinance text and the three months as practice.

Whether a hot shop's furnace exhaust and gas equipment are 'mechanical equipment' whose screening can be approved administratively, or exterior alterations that go to the Commission, is for the Zoning Administrator and Historic Preservation Coordinator to say.
Staff names and personal mailboxes printed on the pages and forms are omitted.
